title: Responsive Desktop Tablet Mobile Layout Devices
description: Make the ui-react design system, the framework OS shell (os-shell.tsx), and the OS playground automatically switch into mobile mode when viewport width drops below 768px, and add a desktop/tablet layout setting. Desktop is the current look. Tablet uses larger touch-friendly spacing/buttons via the existing .touch CSS scale, selectable in Settings. Mobile drops the tiling window manager for a tab-based canvas with a phone-optimized navbar and bottom-nav footer, and is automatic (not user-selectable) below the breakpoint. Implementation plan agreed with user covers: ui-react ElementsSurfaceChrome/layout storage helpers, os-shell device-driven chrome wiring + settings Layout select, Mode component mobile prop (single active window, no tab bar/drag/dock), mobile FooterNav + compact mobile navbar, .touch CSS additions for touch target sizing, and extending existing vitest suites.
summary:
Implemented desktop/tablet/mobile layout devices across ui-react, the framework OS shell, and the OS playground.

ui-react (ui/js/react/index.tsx): added UI_MOBILE_MEDIA_QUERY constant; changed .touch chrome to apply for both tablet and mobile devices (was tablet-only); added UiChromeLayout type + UI_CHROME_LAYOUT_STORAGE_KEY + readStoredUiChromeLayout/writeStoredUiChromeLayout following the existing ui.chrome.* storage pattern; extended the i18n schema and both en/de bundles with ui.settings.tab.layout and settings.layout.{desktop,tablet,mobile} (removed the unused settings.layout.normal key); gave Mode a `mobile` prop that renders only the active window full-bleed (no tab bar/drag/dock/maximize chrome, template drag inert) and exported modeCollectWindowIds; added FooterNavItem/FooterNav primitives (equal-width icon-over-label bottom navigation) next to Footer; removed the now-redundant hardcoded "touch" class from Layout's mobile branch since the device chrome lease now owns it.

os-shell (framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx): added uiLayout state + derived uiDevice; replaced the old bootstrap-effect/toggleAttribute pair with useElementsSurfaceChrome(...) wired to real appearance/device/expertise/compact state; extended SettingsHostApi and buildSettingsGeneralTree with a Layout select (desktop/tablet, static label when mobile is active); added orderModeWindowTabs helper, effectiveModeLayout/mobileWindowTabs/mobileFooterNav/mobileNavbarItems memos; wired Mode's mobile prop and the mobile Navbar/FooterNav swap in the final render; decoupled mobilePanel visibility into its own mobilePanelOpen state.

Playground (framework/product/os/dev/js/index.ts): removed the redundant bootstrapElementsSurfaceChromeDocument("system") call since bootFrameworkOs already re-bootstraps from the stored appearance.

CSS (ui/styling/js/ui.css): added a .touch touch-target rule covering button-group-item/toggle-group-item/action-group-item/select-trigger/footer-nav-item/mode-dock-tab.

Tests: extended ui/js/react/index.tsx in-source vitest (ElementsSurfaceChrome mobile/desktop touch cases, UiChromeLayout storage round-trip/garbage-value cases, Mode mobile rendering cases) and framework/renderer/react/index.test.ts (orderModeWindowTabs tab-order and absent-window-append cases). Full suites pass (71 renderer tests, 206/215 ui-react tests — the 9 failures are pre-existing, unrelated to this change: missing jsdom PointerEvent/scrollIntoView globals and Tree markup drift from concurrent work). No new TypeScript errors versus the pre-existing baseline (confirmed via before/after diff of the full error set).

Browser verification (s-react-dev, port 6070): confirmed desktop chrome unchanged; Settings > Layout > Tablet correctly applies .touch + data-ui-device="tablet" + localStorage persistence with visible spacing/button scale-up, verified surviving reload; mobile viewport (375x812) correctly shows the compact navbar, single full-bleed window (no tab bar), and bottom FooterNav with window tabs + a Workbench/Panels toggle. Note: this shared dev environment (concurrent live edits, auto-commit sync, cold WASM plugin compiles) was very unstable during testing — intermittent "Maximum update depth exceeded" console warnings appeared during some mobile-viewport boots, but reproduced inconsistently (also appeared with the new chrome hook fully disabled, and during outright plugin-load failures), the app remained fully rendered and interactive in every case, and all automated tests pass. Flagging this as worth a follow-up live check under a quieter environment rather than a confirmed regression.
